subtitle: Lesson 9 · Data Structures for AI Work

eyebrow: Key-value pairs, looked up by name
caption: Unlike a list, you look things up by name, not position.

code:
response["missing_key"]             # KeyError! Crashes.
response.get("missing_key")         # None — no crash
response.get("missing_key", "n/a")  # "n/a" — your default
caption: For real API responses, .get() is almost always the safer choice.

code:
for key in response:                  # keys only
    print(key)

for key, value in response.items():   # both together
    print(f"{key}: {value}")
caption: .items() is what you'll reach for most.

eyebrow: Dictionaries ARE how JSON looks in Python
code:
import json

text = '{"model": "gpt-4o", "tokens_used": 142}'
data = json.loads(text)   # now it's a real dict

data["model"]   # "gpt-4o"
caption: Every AI API response in this course arrives exactly this way.
